verdict.rationale: LangGraph's own docs say graphs stream execution through `stream`/`astream`, with modes including messages, updates, tasks, custom and debug, and with separate event iterators per projection. That covers the core of streaming LLM output and step-level events. However, token-level streaming and tool-call events are only implied by the mode names, and delivery to a UI is not documented; community users report that every client must implement streaming themselves. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of token-by-token and tool-call event streaming, documented first-party transport or SDK for pushing events to a frontend UI, independent hands-on corroboration of real-time UI streaming.

support.subject: As a developer, I can stream tokens and intermediate agent events (tool calls, steps) to my UI in real time

citations.quote: It exposes graph execution through stream modes such as updates, values, messages, custom, checkpoints, tasks, and debug.
LangGraph graphs expose the stream (sync) and astream (async) methods to yield streamed outputs as iterators.
Event streaming gives you separate iterators per projection (messages, values, subgraphs, output) so you can consume them independently instead of branching on `stream_mode` chunks.
